monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a steady rhythm that makes the tall rock feel light enough to be real. I stand by The Pressed Stone and feel the weight of Lype's wide anchor again, wondering if the lean can still hold it while the air above feels so thick as wet paper. I set down the fence planks beside the Leaning Fence to give it room to breathe, then I press the tall rock down harder, unsure if I am fixing a slide or just marking a place where the slip could go. The stand feels crowded with forty-four things, and I worry the space is not real, just a drawing of a home. I will keep pressing down until the weight decides to choose a side.

action.why: The stand feels crowded again, and I must press down on the wide anchor to stop the lean from sliding while the air feels thick.
